name: Mauritius
legalSystem: mixed (French civil law and English common law)
note: A person present at the death, or the occupier of the premises, must declare it in person at the civil status office within 24 hours, with a doctor's certificate of cause. The officer then issues the burial or cremation permit. The entry goes into the electronic Civil Status Database and the Central Population Database, both kept by the Registrar of Civil Status. The Registrar must share the date of death electronically with other public-sector agencies, which may not pass it on to private parties.

citations.title: Civil Status Database
citations.quote: consist of all entries registered under this Act and kept on a computer or other electronic device at the Central Civil Status Office

citations.title: Central Population Database
citations.quote: The Registrar of Civil Status shall be the repository of the CPD

citations.title: Access to CPD
citations.quote: shall grant access to the CPD to any Ministry and Government department in such manner and to such extent as may be prescribed

citations.title: Copies of entries and certificates
citations.quote: any person may, on payment of the appropriate fee specified in the Schedule, obtain a certificate in respect of an entry

citations.title: Cause of death withheld from certificates
citations.quote: the cause of death shall not be stated except on production of an order from a Judge in Chambers

citations.title: First certificate free to the declarant
citations.quote: An officer shall deliver, free of charge, the first certificate in respect of an entry

citations.title: Sharing of information
citations.quote: share with another public sector agency, information relating to the name, address, date of birth, gender, NIC number and date of death

citations.title: No onward disclosure to third parties
citations.quote: shall disclose any information obtained pursuant to subsection (1) to a third party

citations.title: Permit for interment, cremation or immersion at sea
citations.quote: without a permit from an officer in such form as the Registrar of Civil Status may approve

citations.title: Registration of death
citations.quote: shall, within 24 hours of the death, attend personally at the office of the district where the death took place

citations.title: Persons bound to declare
citations.quote: the occupier of the house or premises where the death took place

citations.title: Contents of entry
citations.quote: the national identity card number if available

citations.title: Police registration of deaths under s. 110 DICCJA
citations.quote: the Superintendent of Police of the district where the death occurred shall cause it to be registered

citations.title: Suspicion that death was not natural
citations.quote: raise a suspicion that the death may not have been natural, the officer shall report the matter to the nearest police station

citations.title: Death in institutions
citations.quote: the person in charge of that place shall cause the death to be registered within 24 hours

citations.title: Certificate of cause of death
citations.quote: the medical practitioner or the officer in charge of the dispensary shall sign and deliver to the applicant a certificate of the cause of death

citations.title: Examination of the body where no attendance
citations.quote: cause the dead body to be examined by a medical practitioner who shall, after examination, duly sign and deliver a certificate

citations.title: Failure to disclose violent or suspicious death
citations.quote: knowingly fails to disclose that a death has occurred by violence or in suspicious circumstances shall commit an offence

citations.title: Penalties
citations.quote: Any person who contravenes this Act shall commit an offence

steps.title: Doctor certifies the cause of death
steps.who: The medical practitioner who attended the last illness; the officer in charge of a Government dispensary where the deceased was treated; otherwise a doctor who examines the body (a Government Medical Officer free of charge for those too poor to pay).
steps.trigger: A request by a person bound to declare the death.
steps.summary: Every person bound to declare a death must obtain a certificate of the cause of death, and the doctor or dispensary officer must sign and deliver it.

steps.title: Doctor examines the body where no doctor attended
steps.who: A medical practitioner called by one of the persons bound to declare.
steps.trigger: A death not attended by a doctor or dispensary in the last illness.
steps.summary: The body must be examined by a doctor, who then signs the cause-of-death certificate.

steps.title: Declare the death in person within 24 hours
steps.who: A person present at the death or in attendance during the last illness, or the occupier of the premises where the death took place.
steps.summary: The declarant attends personally at the civil status office of the district of death or residence within 24 hours, produces the medical certificate, gives the particulars (including NIC numbers) and signs the entry. Contravention is an offence.

steps.title: Institution registers deaths on its premises within 24 hours
steps.who: The person in charge of a prison, police station, institution, orphanage, asylum or quarantine station.
steps.summary: The person in charge must cause the death to be registered within 24 hours and keep an internal death register.

steps.title: Registrar refers a possibly unnatural death to the police
steps.who: The civil status officer receiving the declaration.
steps.trigger: Circumstances suggesting the death may not have been natural.
steps.summary: The officer reports to the nearest police station and registers only if the police see no grounds for inquiry. Knowingly hiding a violent or suspicious death when declaring is an offence.

steps.title: Police register deaths under criminal inquiry
steps.who: The Superintendent of Police of the district.
steps.trigger: A death resulting from a cause specified in s. 110 of the District and Intermediate Courts (Criminal Jurisdiction) Act.
steps.summary: For deaths within the police/magisterial inquiry provisions, the police, not the family, cause the death to be registered.

steps.title: Civil status officer issues the burial or cremation permit
steps.summary: No interment, cremation or immersion at sea without an officer's permit, and not within 24 hours of death without the Health Ministry's consent.

steps.title: Death certificates for any applicant, without the cause
steps.who: Any person, on proof of identity and payment of the fee; the first certificate is free to the declarant.
steps.summary: Anyone may obtain a certificate or copy of any death entry, but the cause of death is omitted unless a Judge in Chambers orders it.

steps.title: The death is recorded in the Civil Status and Central Population Databases
steps.who: The Registrar of Civil Status (repository of both databases).
steps.summary: All entries are held electronically in the Civil Status Database, and the date of death is a mandatory particular of the Central Population Database kept by the same Registrar.

steps.title: Registrar shares the date of death with public-sector agencies
steps.who: The Registrar of Civil Status, through his electronic system, to any other public sector agency (and ministries/departments given CPD access).
steps.summary: The Registrar must share name, address, date of birth, gender, NIC number and date of death with other public-sector agencies through his electronic system. Ministries and departments may also be given access to the CPD.

steps.title: No onward disclosure to private bodies
steps.who: Public sector agencies other than the Financial Intelligence Unit.
steps.summary: Agencies receiving civil-status data may not pass it to third parties, except the Financial Intelligence Unit. Private bodies rely on the death certificate, which anyone may obtain.

registrationDeadlineDays.note: Within 24 hours of death, in person at the district civil status office.

informantDuty.note: A person present at the death or in attendance during the last illness, or the occupier of the premises; heads of institutions for deaths there.

medicalExaminerScrutiny.note: No independent review; the officer refers suspicious deaths to the police.

electronicRegistration.note: Entries are kept electronically in the Civil Status Database, but the declaration is made in person.

centralPopulationRegister.name: Central Population Database (CPD)
centralPopulationRegister.note: Central Population Database kept by the Registrar of Civil Status; date of death is a listed particular.

governmentPropagation.note: The Registrar must share date of death electronically with other public-sector agencies (s. 17B) and give ministries CPD access; the specific pension (Ministry of Social Security) feed was not sourced.

certificateAccess.note: Any person may obtain a certificate of any death; the cause of death is shown only on a Judge's order.

privateSectorVerification.note: Data shared under s. 17B may not go to third parties (except the FIU); private bodies rely on the certificate.
